h: Weston climbing know-how and coastal extras
p: On a busy holiday, the best way to fit a climb in is to book it early and plan the day around it. Allow a couple of hours for the full visit, including arrival, harness fitting, the safety briefing and your time on the walls.

Before the day, get the participation forms sorted. Each climber needs one, signed by a parent or guardian for under-18s, and it's far quicker online. Have a look at the age guidance when you book, as there's usually a minimum age for climbers and supervision rules for little ones.

A couple of tips for the walls. Use your legs to push up rather than hauling with your arms, and you'll last much longer. And when you reach the top of a jump challenge, focus on the target, take a breath and trust the line. Trainers, comfy clothes and a water bottle are all you need, plus a light snack beforehand rather than a full fish supper.

Weston has plenty more to fill a day. The SeaQuarium on the seafront is a good partner for a wet afternoon, and Weston Museum tells the story of the town and the surrounding area. If the weather's kind, Brean Down, a rugged headland just south of the town and owned by the National Trust, has fantastic views across the Bristol Channel and the remains of an old fort at the tip. Sand Point, to the north, is another great spot for a breezy walk with views across to Wales.
